articles.description:
The Limitations of Lexical Analysis


In the world of static analysis, there is a distinct hierarchy of capability. At the bottom, you have lexical analysis—tools that treat code as a stream of strings. These are your grep-based linters. They are incredibly fast ($O(n)$ where $n$ is characters), but they are structurally blind.
To a regex linter, a function signature is just a pattern to match. It cannot reliably distinguish between a nested closure, a generic type definition, or a comment that looks like code.
When I set out to build DebtDrone, I wanted to measure Cognitive Complexity, not just cyclomatic complexity. Cyclomatic complexity counts paths through code (if/else/switch), but it fails to account for nesting. A flat switch statement with 50 cases is easy to read. A function with …
articles.title: Engineering DebtDrone: Building a High-Performance AST-Based Static Analyzer in Go

Ever wondered how an ATM actually thinks?
No fancy screens.
So I decided to build a fun, functional ATM system in Python—and along the way, I learned how real-world software is structured, secured, and tested.
Let’s break it down 👇
🏧 What Our Python ATM Can Do
This mini ATM system supports:
✅ PIN authentication
All in pure Python, no external libraries.
An ATM doesn’t care who you are.
Correct PIN?
That’s exactly how our Python ATM will behave.
🧠 Step 1: The Brain (Account Data)
Simple. Clear. Effective.
🔐 Step 2: PIN Authentication (The Bouncer)
No correct PIN = no party.
💰 Step 3: Check Balance
Short and sweet.
💸 Step 4: Withdraw Money (With Rules!)
if amount <= 0:
    print("⚠️ Invalid amount")
elif amount > account["balance"]:
    print("❌ Insufficient balance")
else:
    account["balance"] -= amount
    print(f"✅ Withdrawal successful! New balance: Rs {account['balance']}")

No overdrafts. No drama.
💵 Step 5: Deposit Money
if amount <= 0:
    print("⚠️ Invalid amount")
else:
    account["balance"] += amount
    print(f"✅ Deposit successful! New balance: Rs {account['balance']}")

Best feature—money goes in 😄
🧭 Step 6: The ATM Menu (Where the Magic Happens)
    choice = input("Choose an option: ")

    if choice == "1":
        check_balance()
    elif choice == "2":
        withdraw()
    elif choice == "3":
        deposit()
    elif choice == "4":
        print("👋 Thank you for using the ATM")
        break
    else:
        print("⚠️ Invalid choice")

This loop keeps the ATM alive until the user walks away.
🚀 Step 7: Run the ATM
That’s it.
🎯 What This Tiny ATM Teaches You
This simple project covers real software concepts:
🔹 Functions & modular design
These are the same principles used in:
Banking apps
Payment systems
Backend services
🧪 Want to Level It Up?
Try adding:
🔥 Multiple users
Each upgrade moves you closer to real-world app development.
🧠 Final Thought
Building small, fun projects like this ATM isn’t “toy coding.”
If you can build an ATM,
Happy coding 🐍💻
articles.title: I Built a Fun Functional ATM in Python (And It Taught Me More Than I Expected 💳🐍)

This is our third small tool website.
It’s called convertjpgtopng.com, and as the name suggests, it does exactly one thing: convert JPG images to PNG, directly in the browser.
We didn’t build it because we thought the world needed another image converter. There are already plenty of them.
After launching our first two tool sites, we noticed a pattern:
So this time, we intentionally kept things minimal:
No accounts
No pricing pages
No feature list longer than necessary
Upload → convert → download
That’s it.
From a development perspective, this site is part of our ongoing experiments:
If people find it useful, great.
We’re not aggressively promoting it, and we’re not forcing it to be more than what it is. This is a lightweight experiment, and we’re okay letting it grow (or not grow) naturally.
If you ever need to convert a JPG to PNG without installing anything, you can try it here
And if you’re also building small, focused tools instead of big products, I’d genuinely love to hear how that’s working out for you.
articles.title: Our Third Tiny Tool: A Simple JPG to PNG Converter We Built as an Experiment

Mechanische Arbeit des Herzens – Herzfrequenz: messbar? Normal?
Die Herzfrequenz (HF) ist einer der am einfachsten messbaren Parameter der Herzarbeit. Sie beschreibt, wie oft das Herz pro Minute schlägt, nicht jedoch, wie die Arbeit mechanisch oder hämodynamisch erbracht wird.
HF 60 – einfache Messung. Bei einer Herzfrequenz von ca. 60/min dauert eine Herzaktion rund 1000 ms. In 8 Sekunden treten etwa 8 Herzaktionen auf. Die Signalabstätte sind groß, klar trennbar und lassen sich mit einfachen Verkehre zu verläßig auswerten. eine auswertung ist simpel.
HF 148 – Standardmesse. Bei ca. 148/min verkürzt sich die Dauer einer Herzaktion auf etwa 405 ms. In 4 Sekunden liegen bereits 8 Herzaktionen vor. Die Signal rücken enger zusamen, bleiben aber für gängige Algorithmen noch gut erfassbar. Eine…
